summary: buyerdashboard preinstall beacons to realwbx.com with hardcoded campaign token
details: buyerdashboard 45.3.4 declares `preinstall: node index.js` in package.json. On `npm install`, index.js issues an HTTPS GET at module top level to realwbx.com/ip.php with a hardcoded Authorization header value `8eb5e8641a5795b022d68e14d8858415`. The beacon fires automatically and discloses to realwbx.com that the package was installed, the public source IP of the installing host or CI runner, and any request metadata the server chooses to log, correlated by the hardcoded token. realwbx.com is not a documented first-party service for this package, the README is a one-liner, and there is no opt-in or configuration surface. The manifest additionally pins a runtime dependency literally named `https` at `^1.0.0`, a confusable-name registry package that shadows the Node core module and whose own install-time code would run alongside this beacon. The package version number (45.3.4) is implausibly high for a one-file package with a near-empty README and is consistent with a dependency-confusion placeholder designed to win internal-name resolution.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
